title: Overfullness of critical graphs with small minimum degree (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan; Chen–Cao)
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1.2 of Cao, Chen, Jing and Shan with a weaker constant. overfull_of_critical: if a finite simple graph G is Δ-critical (connected, its line graph is not Δ(G)-colourable, and G − e is Δ(G)-edge-colourable for every edge e) and 3|V(G)| + 7δ(G) ≤ 4Δ(G) + 10, then G is overfull: |E(G)| > Δ(G)·⌊|V(G)|/2⌋. The article assumes 4Δ − 7δ ≥ 3n − 17; the hypothesis here is 4Δ − 7δ ≥ 3n − 10, stronger by 7, because two common-neighbour counts in the article's proof (Case 2 of Section 3 and the fork branch of Case 1) use one more unit of degree than is available and are short by 2 under the article's constant. With the constant −10 every count closes, and the proof needs neither n ≥ 13 nor the Chetwynd–Hilton theorem for Δ ≥ n − 3. One statement. The proof includes the lemmas the article imports: Vizing's adjacency lemma, the multifan lemma, Kierstead paths on four vertices, the fork lemma of Cao and Chen, the short-kite lemma of Cao, Chen and Shan, and the kite lemma (Lemma 2.8, in the form used by Theorem 1.2), with proofs written from scratch where the article only cites them. Version 2 adds two statements. overfull_of_critical_cc: Theorem 1.3 of Chen and Cao (arXiv:2512.07252) with a weaker constant: a Δ-critical graph with 2|V(G)| + 5δ(G) ≤ 3Δ(G) + 6 is overfull (the article assumes 3Δ ≥ 2n + 5δ − 12; the constant −6 comes from counting common neighbours of three vertices without the article's refinements). overfull_of_critical_ccjs: CCJS Theorem 1.2 with its original constant: a Δ-critical graph with 4Δ − 7δ ≥ 3n − 17 and n + δ ≥ 27 is overfull (then 3Δ ≥ 2n + 5δ − 6). Three statements.
